en.title: Maximum Calories Jumping from the Ground to Visit All Stones
en.description:
The ground has height 0. You must jump off from the ground and visit every stone exactly once in any order, and you cannot return to the ground. Each jump contributes the square of the height difference between its start and end, and the total contribution should be maximized. Different stones with the same height must still each be visited once.

The standard I/O, examples and solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains the stone heights. 1≤n≤100000, 1≤height≤46340.
en.explanation: Example 1: the order 0→3→1→2 gives calories 9+4+1=14. Example 2: the only jump 0→5 contributes 25. Example 3: first jump from 0 to 2 for 4; the remaining jumps between equal heights give 0, for a total of 4.
hints: Sort the heights and visit the remaining highest, lowest, second highest, second lowest, and so on, adding the squared adjacent differences, including the first jump from 0.
